strengths: Correctly anchors the endothelial lineage using VWF, TIE1, FLT1, EDN1, CALCRL, PRCP, FOXF1.
Recognizes the aerocyte/pulmonary capillary signature (SLC6A4, AOC2, EMID1, KIRREL3, HYAL2, SLCO4A1, PRX, AGER).
Excludes alveolar epithelial and immune alternatives despite AGER/CCL3 presence.
weaknesses: Top1 remains the broader CL:0000115 even though the same evidence supports the descendant CL:4028001.
Top-ranked markers include non-endothelial genes (SMG8, CCL3, ciliary genes) without fully explaining their presence.

strengths: Conservative and correctly mapped to the exact majority CLID CL:0000115.
Consistent with canonical endothelial evidence from the same marker list.
weaknesses: Does not capture the pulmonary capillary specialization supported by SLC6A4/AOC2/EMID1/KIRREL3/HYAL2/SLCO4A1/PRX/AGER.
Ignores granularity available in the original marker evidence.

strengths: Explicitly proposes the pulmonary capillary endothelial subtype, matching the supported aerocyte signature.
Correctly prioritizes VWF, TIE1, ROBO3, KIRREL3, EMID1, CALCRL for endothelial identity.
Reasonably excludes immune and epithelial candidates based on absence of CD3D/CD68/EPCAM.
weaknesses: Top1 label 'Pulmonary vascular endothelial cell (likely capillary endothelial subtype)' is non-canonical and unmapped.
Candidate list includes alveolar epithelial/fibroblast options, creating ambiguity even though those are unsupported.
Mapping status was 'review', so CL:4028001 was only a registry candidate rather than a deterministic exact match.

supporting: VWF, TIE1, FLT1, EDN1, GPER1, CALCRL, PRCP, FOXF1 are canonical endothelial markers and establish the dominant endothelial lineage.

SLC6A4, AOC2, EMID1, KIRREL3, HYAL2, SLCO4A1, PRX, AGER form an aerocyte/pulmonary capillary endothelial signature, directly supporting the added capillary/pulmonary components of CL:4028001 (PMID 31840817).
Absence of EPCAM, CD3D, and CD68 and lack of a broad AT1/AT2 program exclude the alveolar epithelial candidate despite shared AGER expression.
conflicting: Top-ranked non-endothelial DEGs (SMG8, CCL3, GPN2, NIPSNAP1, SPATA42, DNAH1, CFAP221, DYNLT2B, LRRIQ3) create minor noise and a possible low-level ciliated/immune signal.
AGER is also a classical alveolar type 1 marker, but the overall combination of aerocyte markers favors pulmonary capillary endothelium over alveolar epithelium.
enrichment_or_literature: Reactome terms (Intrinsic Pathway of Fibrin Clot Formation, Glycosaminoglycan metabolism, SLC-mediated transmembrane transport) are consistent with endothelial/vascular biology but are not lineage-specific.
PMID 31840817 supports the pulmonary capillary/aerocyte interpretation of the observed marker combination in human lung.
